description:
Companion code and data for the manuscript "Triplet architecture enables deep error-minimization of the genetic code" (submitted to Journal of Molecular Evolution).

This archive contains a Monte Carlo framework that quantifies error-minimization in the standard genetic code (SGC) using two graph-theoretic metrics on the codon Hamming graph: Dirichlet energy (the unweighted graph Laplacian quadratic form) and receiver noise distortion, both scored against 8 PCA-derived amino acid physicochemical properties retaining 97.1% of variance.

A 2 x 2 factorial design crosses codon length (n = 2 versus n = 3) with alphabet size (10 versus 20 amino acids). Each condition is scored against a degeneracy-preserving null model of 1,000,000 random codes generated by permuting amino acid labels among sense codons while holding per-amino-acid codon counts fixed.

Principal results. The SGC outperforms all 1,000,000 matched-degeneracy random codes on both metrics (noise distortion z = -16.6; Dirichlet energy z = -14.6; p < 10^-6). A 10-amino-acid doublet projection remains inside its null tail (z = -3.8, with the best random doublet at z = -4.0), whereas a 10-amino-acid triplet code lies beyond its null (z = -14.8). Triplet architecture therefore crosses an optimization threshold that doublet architecture does not, independently of alphabet size. The mechanism is synonymy at the wobble position: position 3 absorbs 69-77% of single-nucleotide errors as synonymous substitutions.

Note that the null distributions at n = 2 and n = 3 operate over code spaces of differing size and degeneracy, so z-score differences across architectures are directional indicators rather than strictly commensurable quantities.

Contents. Simulation source (src/), the factorial and sensitivity drivers (run_*.py), figure-generation scripts (figures/), the regression test suite (tests/), canonical numerical outputs (results/*.json), supplementary tables, the manuscript and supplementary text, and a portable CSV export of the raw null distributions (share/, three files of 1,000,000 (D, E) rows) sufficient to regenerate every figure and z-score without rerunning the Monte Carlo. The 46 MB binary null_distributions.npz is excluded by design and is reproducible from run_publication_controls.py.
